SPN-1112-01: Samsung aims for early 2027 to develop 3D Cube-H hybrid bonding, with a 6 µm interconnect pitch for stacking AI processors and HBM.
SPN-1112-02: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after 33 years; CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO; stock fell 13%.
SPN-1112-03: Whitepaper on oxide removal, cleaning and activation for power-electronics assembly.
SPN-1112-04: imec CEO says AI pushes innovation toward system-level integration of logic, memory, photonics and packaging.
SPN-1112-05: Samsung and SK hynix watch Nvidia's leadership uncertainty but expect existing supply deals to stay largely unaffected.
SPN-1112-06: Credo shows micro-emitter optics and a 1.6T active light cable with copper-level reliability over 50 m at OCP 2026.
SPN-1112-07: Diamond Foundry makes a first 200 mm single-crystal diamond wafer, aimed at AI-chip cooling.
SPN-1112-08: TSMC sets up a US$500 million investment company to take stakes in chip-ecosystem firms.
SPN-1112-09: TSMC plans to invest up to US$1 billion in OpenAI and Anthropic plus a strategic investment arm (SCMP view of what it gains).
SPN-1112-10: AMD and Samsung develop embedded processors (EPYC Embedded 9006) with up to 1.8x throughput.
SPN-1112-11: Siemens will acquire Lauterbach to add chip verification and software debugging to its EDA portfolio.
SPN-1112-12: University of Tokyo makes p-type boron carbon nitride on a 2-inch wafer for complementary 2D electronics.
SPN-1112-13: Musk's Terafab targets 1 million wafers per month after 2032, 700,000 of them memory.
SPN-1113-01: IP integration risk is rising with complex SoCs and chiplets; experts call for better specs, cross-block verification, IP management and AI-assisted testing.
SPN-1113-02: Edge AI inference drives memory architectures that cut data movement: processing-in-memory and near-memory computing.
SPN-1113-03: Paper: metal TIM warpage simulations fail with bulk material data; rheometer-derived film data improves accuracy.
SPN-1113-04: EE Times reports Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO and the task of finding a successor.
SPN-1113-05: CNBC reports an investigation alleging an Alice Huang link to Huawei-linked firms, raising export-control concerns.
SPN-1113-06: Nvidia's turmoil lifts AMD and Broadcom shares as investors expect customers to diversify.
SPN-1113-07: Hon Hai Q3 net profit up 34% to NT$77.52 billion on AI server demand.
SPN-1113-08: CNBC discusses Nvidia's succession uncertainty and investor confidence despite record growth.
SPN-1113-09: Larger models and longer context strain memory capacity, bandwidth, latency, power and cost; compute, interconnect and software must be co-planned.
SPN-1113-10: Agentic AI automates semiconductor engineering workflows and widens design exploration while humans keep oversight and verification.
SPN-1113-11: Arm adds FP8 support; an FPMR register switches between E4M3 and E5M2 formats to cut memory, power and latency.
SPN-1113-12: AI-driven design favors parallelism and power efficiency; experts discuss RISC-V as a flexible open base for AI accelerators.
SPN-1116-01: At electronica 2026 chipmakers stress system-level platforms: MCUs with NPUs, agentic tools, power electronics, vertical power delivery, GaN for data centers.
SPN-1116-02: ASE invests NT$100 billion in two Kaohsiung plants for advanced AI chip packaging, targeting NT$80 billion annual revenue and 5,000 jobs.
SPN-1116-03: Paper: hybrid and fusion wafer bonding underpin both 'More than Moore' heterogeneous integration and 'More Moore' transistor scaling.
SPN-1116-04: Weekly roundup: manufacturing, chiplet integration, automotive processors, AI hardware and Nvidia-related export scrutiny.
SPN-1116-05: TSMC received a record NT$167.586 billion in subsidies from US, Japan, Germany and China in the first nine months of 2026.
SPN-1116-06: Opinion: Taiwan's 'silicon shield' is no guarantee; defense resilience also needed.
SPN-1116-07: US House Speaker cites growing consensus for tighter AI chip export curbs to China.
SPN-1116-08: Experts expect little disruption to Taiwan's supply chain from Huang's exit; ASIC and AMD diversification may speed up; CUDA keeps Nvidia entrenched.
SPN-1116-09: Germanium doping improves electron movement in alpha-gallium oxide films without hurting thermal conductivity (power electronics).
SPN-1116-10: Analysts: no immediate disruption for TSMC, Samsung, ASUS; long-term roadmap concerns remain.
SPN-1116-11: Singapore faces scrutiny over suspected Nvidia chip smuggling to China and a US$390 million fraud case.
SPN-1116-12: GlobalFoundries breaks ground on a US$10 billion fab in Malta, New York.
SPN-1117-01: AI agents automate customization, verification and optimization in chip design; orchestration, security, privacy and reliability must improve first.
SPN-1117-02: SMIC sees tight capacity through 2027, maybe into 2H28; equipment lead times 16-24 months.
SPN-1117-03: Paper: alkaline wet etch for Al and AlCu as a PAN-free alternative.
SPN-1117-04: TRIUMF accelerator supports semiconductor materials analysis and radiation testing.
SPN-1117-05: US Treasury Secretary urges Nvidia's board to appoint external leadership and probe alleged smuggling.
SPN-1117-06: US requires licences for overseas data centres serving Chinese firms, closing a cloud loophole.
SPN-1117-07: With memory scarce, better test, repair and reliability raise usable die supply across SRAM, DRAM and HBM.
SPN-1117-08: Opinion: export controls may speed China's domestic AI development.
SPN-1117-09: AI-powered three-layer sensor works as a compact spectrometer, cutting reconstruction error 95.6%.
SPN-1117-10: Opinion: Huang's exit shows Asia's dependence on one US company.
SPN-1117-11: Opinion: governments tighten export controls and secure supply chains as China pursues chip independence.
SPN-1118-01: India expands IC packaging: Vishay, Kaynes, Paras Semiconductors and BroadPak launch joint ventures and facilities.
SPN-1118-02: OSAT market forecast at US$80.2 billion by 2033 (market-research press release).
SPN-1118-03: Paper: LAB, R-LAB and R-LTC flip-chip bonding for AI/HPC chiplet packages.
SPN-1118-04: Nvidia posts record revenue, raises FY2028 growth outlook to 75% and secures memory, substrate and packaging capacity with TSMC's help.
SPN-1118-05: Samsung reportedly develops custom HBM4E for Meta, with customer functions in a 2 nm base die.
SPN-1118-06: Editorial: Taiwan stays vital to AI supply chain despite Huang's exit; risks are delayed servers and volatility.
SPN-1118-07: Nvidia forms a board committee on national security and export controls.
SPN-1118-08: Optical computing gains momentum as AI inference demands energy efficiency; startups build photonic chips.
SPN-1118-09: Intesa Sanpaolo uses quantum-inspired algorithms on GPUs for ATM cash planning (off-topic for IC design).
SPN-1118-10: Lam Research's David Fried on blending physics and data in simulation for angstrom-level control, memory and advanced packaging.
SPN-1118-11: imec opens a Japan R&D base at Hokkaido University: 15 researchers over five years on photonic ICs and packaging.
SPN-1118-12: Nvidia warns buyers of legal risks and plans limits on GPU rental to Chinese businesses.
SPN-1119-01: SPIL partners with Nvidia to triple Taiwan advanced packaging capacity by mid-2029; Nvidia invests over US$1 billion in Kinsus for substrates.
SPN-1119-02: TrendForce: new US AI chip export rules tighten compliance for Taiwan foundries and packaging firms, risking order delays.
SPN-1119-03: Paper: AI-powered X-ray inspection moves from defect detection toward proactive intelligence.
SPN-1119-04: Microsoft CEO admits inadequate testing contributed to a global Outlook outage (off-topic).
SPN-1119-05: Nvidia stops shipping licensed Hopper AI chips to China.
SPN-1119-06: Taiwanese economists warn of supply-chain and margin effects from Nvidia's leadership change.
SPN-1119-07: Nvidia says it can thrive without Huang, rejects his return, raises forecasts and buybacks.
SPN-1119-08: Academia Sinica experts see Nvidia's change as part of US-China supply-chain restructuring.
SPN-1119-09: Anthropic prices IPO at US$83 per share, raising US$81.3 billion (off-topic for IC design).
SPN-1119-10: Synopsys, Hiveware, Silvaco and Axiomise discuss AI agents in chip design: integration, keeping expertise, data protection and cost.
SPN-1119-11: South Korea nears US$1 trillion in exports on a chip boom, but small firms see limited benefit.
SPN-1120-01: Intel signs its first external 18A-P foundry customer and names Microsoft as first customer for EMIB packaging.
SPN-1120-02: TSMC buys a 0.03% stake in Anthropic for US$500 million at the US$83 IPO price.
SPN-1120-03: Paper: EOTPR fine-pitch probing isolates die-to-die interconnect defects in chiplet devices.
SPN-1120-04: TSMC halts advanced-node (below 16 nm) orders from Chinese chipmakers without US licences.
SPN-1120-05: Cal Newport argues superintelligence is improbable (opinion; off-topic).
SPN-1120-06: SEMI expects silicon wafer shipments to grow 11.8% in 2026 on AI, memory and fab expansion.
SPN-1120-07: Nvidia reports record Q3 revenue of US$115.8 billion under interim CEO.
SPN-1120-08: IEA: data center electricity use could double to 1,000 TWh by 2030.
SPN-1120-10: Silvaco plasma-chamber simulation links kinetic plasma and feature-scale models to predict etch profiles.
SPN-1120-11: Detachable fiber connectors for co-packaged and near-packaged optics face standardization and assembly challenges.
SPN-1120-12: AI aids manufacturing, but autonomous control is limited by data gaps and validation needs.
SPN-1123-01: Intel Foundry describes joining measurement data, AI analytics and industry standards to raise yield and move toward autonomous production.
SPN-1123-02: Tesla trims the memory of its AI4.5 chip from 32GB to 24GB because memory costs are rising, moving to LPDDR5X; similar cuts for AI5 and AI6 aim to save cost and protect supply for Optimus.
SPN-1123-04: Weekly roundup: Intel signed its first external 18A-P customer, Siemens bought Breker, US export limits on China tightened, Nvidia is ramping packaging, Europe commits €33B to chip projects.
SPN-1123-05: Taipei Times editorial argues that government ownership stakes in companies bias US export-control decisions, and calls for divestment to keep regulators neutral.
SPN-1123-06: Nagare Labs, backed by Pat Gelsinger, is developing Z2RAM, a vertically stacked memory that claims SRAM-like speed with higher density, aimed at AI accelerators.
SPN-1123-07: Pat Gelsinger says Europe should stop chasing advanced chipmaking and back emerging technologies; Playground Global works with France's CEA to turn lab research into companies.
SPN-1123-08: Researchers tune the wavelength and polarization of infrared light by twisting two atomically thin semiconductor layers.
SPN-1123-09: Chinese security firm Qi An Xin expands AI-driven cyber defence (Aisoc platform) as automated attacks grow.
SPN-1123-10: Alibaba plans to rely mainly on its own T-Head AI chips after 2027 because tighter US export controls threaten supply; quarterly revenue up 10%, profit up 207%.
SPN-1123-11: Measuring silicon margin under varying workloads (PVTW) goes beyond pass/fail and helps target production tests.
SPN-1123-12: AI accelerators need high current at low voltage, pushing power delivery to vertical designs with voltage regulators integrated near the processor.
SPN-1123-13: Virtual twins plus machine learning model process variation to improve DRAM yield, with predicted yield rising from 0.1% to 78.5%.
SPN-1124-01: TSMC sees strong AI chip demand despite market worries, keeps investing in capacity, took a stake in Anthropic and tightens chip exports to China.
SPN-1124-02: Experts from Cadence, Synopsys, universities and AI startups say AI is changing chip design and verification work, and universities are updating curricula.
SPN-1124-03: Amkor's S-SWIFT packaging uses an embedded-trace RDL process to give die-to-die links more bandwidth for AI, HPC and data-center chips.
SPN-1124-04: Pat Gelsinger says Moore's Law is not dead and calls for a 10,000-fold efficiency gain through light, power, cooling, materials and packaging.
SPN-1124-05: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO after briefly removing him over alleged ties to a suspected Chinese spy; shares rose 25% premarket.
SPN-1124-06: US threats against firms building overseas data centers and tighter export controls push other governments to diversify AI suppliers and build sovereign computing.
SPN-1124-07: AI speeds up scientific research but raises concerns about transparency, strained peer review and the role of human researchers.
SPN-1124-08: SoftBank explored a $1 trillion purchase of SK Hynix but dropped it over financial and regulatory hurdles; it shows Masayoshi Son wants control of the AI supply chain including memory.
SPN-1124-09: Diamond Foundry made the first 200mm single-crystal diamond wafer, meant to spread heat from AI chips and lower hotspot temperatures.
SPN-1124-10: China's chip exports rose 108% in 2026, about double South Korea's growth, driven by AI, chips, EVs and advanced manufacturing.
SPN-1124-11: Under Prime Minister Takaichi, Japan uses investment in chips, AI, energy and supply chains to build regional influence and offer Southeast Asia an alternative to US-China rivalry.
SPN-1124-12: Mass spectrometry can monitor trace gas impurities at parts-per-trillion levels in fabs to protect yield and quality.
SPN-1124-13: Fab design now plans tool integration early and works with suppliers so the fab stays adaptable and lower risk.
SPN-1125-01: Editorial on Japan's upgraded 56-qubit quantum computer: the next challenge is commercialization amid global competition.
SPN-1125-02: AI can help chip-design productivity, but needs scalable data management, good data, IP security and real domain understanding to work in practice.
SPN-1125-03: As packages get denser, alpha-particle emission becomes a growing soft-error reliability risk for AI and HPC packages.
SPN-1125-04: MIT Energy Initiative marks 20 years of work on decarbonization, renewable supply, grid resilience and sustainable fuels.
SPN-1125-05: Edge AI, robotics and sensors are driving autonomous farming with real-time crop monitoring.
SPN-1125-06: Huang's return lifted AI stocks, but Southeast Asian data-center growth still faces regulatory, financial and geopolitical limits.
SPN-1125-07: A new UL 1741 certification program could make vehicle-to-grid power feeding easier to adopt.
SPN-1125-08: AI can speed up derivative chip designs, but physical constraints, missing data and changing workflows mean human experts are still needed to judge feasibility and cost.
SPN-1125-09: AI tools struggle to produce implementable RTL that meets power and performance targets, while high-level synthesis stays strong in productivity and verification.
SPN-1125-10: Photonic design must be judged at system level because parts that each meet spec can behave differently once combined into an optical link.
SPN-1125-11: Arteris analysed 1,000 silicon design starts and finds rising system complexity, AI-driven growth and growing importance of interconnects.
SPN-1125-12: The AI compute race is lifting demand for GPUs, memory, packaging and data centers, reshaping supply chains and raising energy use.
SPN-1125-13: Nvidia's CEO change, AI-chip export scrutiny and ongoing rare-earth shortages from China add uncertainty to global chip supply and trade.
